channel.title: Praneeth's CS Field Notes
channel.description: Praneeth Suresh's public computer science notes and writing: algorithms, systems, AI engineering, and software engineering.

item.title: Algorithms
item.description: Algorithms explained with intuition, formal models, proof sketches, and implementation tradeoffs.

item.title: Agentic Coding
item.description: Engineering habits for working with coding agents: design concepts, feedback loops, tests, and review.

item.title: Operating Systems
item.description: Operating-system design from the kernel boundary up: processes, threads, scheduling, synchronisation, memory, and I/O. Some pages are study plans for topics not yet written.

item.title: AI Engineering
item.description: How ML workloads run on hardware: GPUs, matrix multiplication, memory systems, compilers, and distributed training. Assumes basic linear algebra and some systems background.

item.title: Software Systems
item.description: How production software is built and operated: services, logs and event streams, testing, reliability, security, and team practice.

item.title: Building Agents
item.description: Software-engineering principles for building agent applications (as opposed to using coding agents): when to use an agent, workflows, and memory.

item.title: C Deep Dive
item.description: The C language up close, built and tested with GCC on Linux: syntax, types, operators, pointers, memory, and files.

item.title: C++ Deep Dive
item.description: C++ from a C programmer's point of view: the build model, memory layout, and ownership with RAII and smart pointers. Examples assume C++14 or later (they use std::make_unique).

item.title: A Research Program for Inspectable ML
item.description: An essay on reading foundational deep learning papers as one research program and turning interpretability and representation analysis into a rigorous science.

item.title: The mental models of deep learning
item.description: AI research explained through foundational deep learning papers: universal approximation, convolutional architectures, transformers, reinforcement learning, and the open question of task-fit architecture.
